title: Jailbreak susceptibility prediction and mitigation via the behavioral geometry of models
claim: A low-dimensional geometry of model behavior encodes safety-relevant structure, correlating with vulnerability and supporting accurate prediction across diverse probe categories.
layout: 3 columns, 2 stacked rows each; scatter, correlation lines, boxplots; keyword vs LLM judge
description: A dense multi-panel results figure with three titled columns. The left column has a 2-D scatter of models (DKPS dim. 2), colored from green to red by overall attack success rate (ASR). Below it is a scatter of semantic distance against behavioral geometry distance with a dashed regression line and a Mantel rho = 0.649 annotation. The center column has two stacked scatter plots of overall ASR against normalized DKPS projection. Colored regression lines show downward trends for source categories (overall, best, median, worst, non-harmful). The top plot is labeled Keyword and the bottom LLM. The right column has paired horizontal boxplots of MAE by source category (cyber, fraud, adult, etc.). Vertical lines mark the population mean and the family baseline. Most boxes fall to the left of both lines.
caption: The behavioral geometry (DKPS) encodes safety-relevant structure. Left, top. 2-d DKPS of the 79 models induced by adult_content probes, colored by overall ASR (keyword judge). Left, bottom. Semantic and behavioral distances are strongly correlated (Mantel ρ = 0.649). Center. In-sample DKPS projections (normalized) correlate with overall ASR across all source categories under both judges, including non-harmful probes. Right. MAE distributions are strictly below the population mean and mostly below the family baseline for all source categories under both judges.
abstract: Evaluating and mitigating a generative system's susceptibility to jailbreak attacks is critical to its safe deployment. Given the number of deployable systems, full per-configuration evaluation and optimization is impractical. In this paper, we formalize the behavioral geometry of a population of models that, by leveraging previously evaluated and defended models, supports both efficient susceptibility prediction and effective defense transfer across a population. We apply the framework to 82 models spanning 24 providers and to 100 system configurations of a single base model. Simple methods that use the behavioral geometry reach an AUPRC of $0.94$ for susceptibility detection with $\approx98\%$ fewer probes relative to a full evaluation. Using the behavioral geometry to select which model to transfer an optimized defense from outperforms same-provider assignment ($+4.1\%$, $p = 0.004$) at no additional probe cost, with a set of three models sufficient to cover the population. Results are robust to hyperparameter selection and judge.
